title: Measured MoE prefill tile padding: 12800 padded rows for 10240 real (1.25x)
verdict: the padded row space is measured, not modelled; 25% of the gate/up WMMA work at the production chunk is padding
quant: mixed GGUF: Q4_K gate/up experts, Q5_1 down experts, Q5_K 2 tensors, Q8_0 5 tensors

how_measured.instrument: rocprofv3 --kernel-trace on the production prefill window at risk multiplier 4.0
how_measured.derivation: gguf_q4_k_selected_dual_wmma_iu8_risk_prefill_kernel launches dim3 grid = ((out_features_total + 127) / 128, wmma_total_rows / TILE_ROWS) with dim3 block = 128 threads (gguf_q4_k_selected_prefill.hip:2471-2478). rocprofv3 reports Grid_Size as total work-items, so the block count in Y equals Grid_Size_Y and wmma_total_rows = Grid_Size_Y x 16. Cross-check on the same launch: out_features_total = 1280 gives 10 column blocks, and Grid_Size_X = 1280 = 10 x 128 threads, which confirms the work-item interpretation.
how_measured.observed: Grid_Size_Y = 800 for all 1504 launches of the q4_k gate/up risk owner in the window

arithmetic.experts_with_a_tile: 800 tiles over 512 experts: if x experts hold one tile and 512-x hold two, x + 2(512-x) = 800 gives x = 224. So 224 experts have at most 16 rows and 288 have 17-32. Fewer than 512 experts hold rows, which is why the real distribution pads less than uniform routing would.

correction_to_prior_estimate.prior: A modelled uniform-routing estimate in worklog/entries/20261003T235118.067749Z-lhl-qwen4exp-moe-tile-padding-8a6b02.md put the production chunk at 16384 padded rows for 10240 real, i.e. 1.60x.
correction_to_prior_estimate.now: 1.25x, measured. Real top-10 routing is sparser than uniform - 224 of 512 experts hold at most one tile - so the modelled figure was pessimistic by 0.35x of work ratio.
correction_to_prior_estimate.direction: the finding stands; its size is smaller than modelled

mechanism: group_scatter.hip:350 rounds every expert owning at least one row up to a full 16-row WMMA tile, and gguf_q4_k_selected_prefill.hip:2472 turns that padded total into the launched grid. Rows beyond a tile boundary are recomputed as padding.

prize.note: Upper bound only. Eliminating padding entirely would take the gate/up row space from 12800 to 10240, a 20% reduction in gate/up WMMA work. Whether any of that is recoverable depends on finding a row space that packs tail rows from multiple experts into shared tiles, which needs a kernel able to switch weight pointers mid-tile or a tail path cheaper than 1/4 of the WMMA path - the exact grouped fallback is not it (it already loses by median +157.8% while doing 1.25x less work).

limits: One host (gfx1151 APU), one model, one quant, one case (code-p4096), one chunk size, one execution profile.
Single prompt: the routing distribution is prompt-dependent, so 1.25x is this prompt's figure and not a general one. A sparse-routing prompt would pad more.
The 12800 figure is the padded row space the kernel is launched over; it is not itself a timing.
No correctness gate applies: no arithmetic changed and no default was modified.
